method.input_enumeration: git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all with GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0; deleted/nonregular files are not read
method.secret_patterns: The six named regex definitions were read with Python AST/literal evaluation from scan_git_secret_markers.py, without executing the archived-history scanner. Additional AWS session-key, Slack, Stripe-live, credential URL, Authorization, JWT and URL-query markers were applied.
method.additional_literal_check: Quoted values at credential-named assignments were flagged after selected explicit-placeholder/environment-reference exclusions; matching values were never printed or retained in this receipt.
method.private_output_checks: Known private-config/key filename markers and Android logcat/emulator diagnostic text markers; scoped review of the listed device evidence directories and structured machine metadata.
method.binary_review: Selected raw-byte markers were checked in the five binary files. Every non-directory member of the three ZIPs was read in memory, never extracted or executed; archive path/encryption checks were also inspected.
method.stability: Re-enumerated status paths and rehashed every read regular file after the scan; both checks held for this particular observation.
method.fingerprint_encoding: SHA256 of Python json.dumps(list(file_sha256.items())).encode(), preserving captured order. It is not a fingerprint of the later attribution-modified checkout.

limitations: No comprehensive or entropy-based secret detector was used. Unknown, encoded, split, obfuscated or low-entropy credentials can evade these markers; absence of matches is not absence of secrets.
Ignored/untracked caches, private machine files and build outputs outside the status inventory were not recursively scanned. Git history and remote state were outside this development-worktree scan.
Only 903 regular-file hashes were captured for 905 status entries; the two deleted entries contributed counts but their old bytes were not scanned.
Binary marker scanning and reading ZIP members are not semantic execution, decompilation, malware scanning or proof of complete archive/dependency licensing.
The raw logs here are deliberately retained bounded build/test evidence. The name/content checks do not certify that every possible personal identifier is absent.
The synthetic-looking quoted-credential hit is documented as a test-context diagnostic, not silently treated as a real leak or a complete private adjudication.
The initial path-context review preceded the final 905-path scan; this report preserves both scopes and does not claim that an earlier context inspection checked later edits.

The record was archived later. Attribution comments and subsequent development can change the listed source hashes; consumers must compare exact hashes or run a fresh scan rather than treating this receipt as current.
Source attribution, runtime correctness, release readiness, action/deployment containment and publishing authorization are separate checks. This diagnostic authorizes none of them.
